before: A Cargo package has a manifest and one or more targets such as a binary or library crate. Edition selects language rules; it is not the compiler version. This fixture explicitly chooses edition2024 and only a local library dependency.

Save the files below, put the complete main example in src/main.rs, then run cargo run --offline --quiet from the package directory. path points to supplied local source rather than a registry. Offline does not conjure missing dependencies: all required sources must already be present.
```toml
# Cargo.toml
[package]
name = "lesson_app"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2024"
[dependencies]
lesson_math = { path = "localmath" }
```
```toml
# localmath/Cargo.toml
[package]
name = "lesson_math"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2024"
```
```rust
// localmath/src/lib.rs
pub fn double(n: u32) -> u32 { n * 2 }
```

Complete local Rust example; the app itself does not execute it:
```rust
fn main() { println!("{}", lesson_math::double(6)); }
```
Expected output or behavior: 12. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Compare the language edition with the actual rustc version rather than treating them as interchangeable. You may trace it without a Rust compiler; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: Cargo is Rust's project tool. It can connect an app to a library in a nearby folder.
